article.title: Three new species of Lycianthes (Solanaceae) from Panama
article.authors: Ellen Dean, Jennifer Poore, and Hannah Kang
article.citation: Dean, Ellen, Poore, Jennifer, Kang, Hannah (2020): Three new species of Lycianthes (Solanaceae) from Panama. Phytotaxa 471 (2): 113-126.
article.license: Unknown; item-level reuse rights for article text, PDF, and figures were not verified.

claimPolicy: Claims are concise English paraphrases of one exact Plazi description-extension row each. They retain the publication's stated comparison, localities, habitat, elevation, and voucher-month scope; they do not assert global range, full phenology, or whole-species variation. The DOI source is cited bibliographically with unknown item-level rights; no article prose, PDF, or figure is reproduced.

records.sourceName: Lycianthes coloradensis E. Dean and H. Kang

morphology.text: In the treatment's comparison with Lycianthes purpusii, L. coloradensis is distinguished by star-shaped hairs whose rays are often rebranched, shorter calyx appendages, nearly equal stamens, and smaller reported fruit (up to 12 mm long and 15 mm in diameter).
morphology.placeTimeScope: Comparative diagnosis in the 2020 taxonomic treatment, pages 116-117. The traits are stated relative to L. purpusii and are not estimates of variation across all populations.
morphology.lifeStatus: The claim is bounded to the taxonomic material discussed in the diagnosis; the paragraph does not characterize the provenance or life status of every individual.

distribution.text: The treatment reports L. coloradensis as endemic to Panama, with localities associated with the Ngäbe-Buglé comarca and the historical Bocas del Toro–Chiriquí provincial boundary.
distribution.placeTimeScope: As-published distribution statement in the 2020 treatment, pages 116-117; it is not a current exhaustive range survey or an independently validated range map.
distribution.lifeStatus: The article's endemicity and locality wording is reported as attributed; the source does not separately classify every occurrence as wild, cultivated, or escaped.

ecology.text: The article associates reported records with lower montane rainforest, cloud forest, and disturbed primary forest at 1,100-2,200 m elevation.
ecology.placeTimeScope: Habitat and elevation reported for the treatment's cited localities in Panama, pages 116-117; this is not a complete ecological niche or sampling envelope.
ecology.lifeStatus: The treatment describes forest settings and taxonomic collections; it does not assess cultivated or escaped populations.

lifeHistory.text: The treatment reports flowering specimens collected in April and May and mature-fruit specimens collected from March through November.
lifeHistory.placeTimeScope: Collection-month summary for specimens cited in the 2020 treatment, pages 116-117; collection months do not establish continuous or complete annual phenology.
lifeHistory.lifeStatus: The statement concerns dated taxonomic specimens; population status and complete seasonal coverage were not assessed.

records.sourceName: Lycianthes fortunensis J. Poore & E. Dean

morphology.text: In its comparison with Lycianthes multiflora, the treatment distinguishes L. fortunensis by a rounded flower-bud tip, an elongated scarious and lobed calyx margin, and absence of calyx appendages.
morphology.placeTimeScope: Comparative diagnosis in the 2020 taxonomic treatment, pages 118-121. The traits are stated relative to L. multiflora and are not estimates of variation across all populations.
morphology.lifeStatus: The claim is bounded to the taxonomic material discussed in the diagnosis; the paragraph does not characterize the provenance or life status of every individual.

distribution.text: The treatment reports L. fortunensis as endemic to Panama, with localities in Chiriquí, Veraguas, and the Ngäbe-Buglé comarca; an earlier locality was recorded under Bocas del Toro Province.
distribution.placeTimeScope: As-published distribution statement in the 2020 treatment, pages 118-121; it is not a current exhaustive range survey or an independently validated range map.
distribution.lifeStatus: The article's endemicity and locality wording is reported as attributed; the source does not separately classify every occurrence as wild, cultivated, or escaped.

ecology.text: The article associates reported records with cloud and premontane forests, often on slopes or beside roads and trails, at 730-1,645 m elevation.
ecology.placeTimeScope: Habitat and elevation reported for the treatment's cited localities in Panama, pages 118-121; this is not a complete ecological niche or sampling envelope.
ecology.lifeStatus: The treatment describes forest settings and taxonomic collections; it does not assess cultivated or escaped populations.

lifeHistory.text: The treatment reports flowering specimens collected from February through April and mature-fruit specimens collected from January through September.
lifeHistory.placeTimeScope: Collection-month summary for specimens cited in the 2020 treatment, pages 118-121; collection months do not establish continuous or complete annual phenology.
lifeHistory.lifeStatus: The statement concerns dated taxonomic specimens; population status and complete seasonal coverage were not assessed.

records.sourceName: Lycianthes talamancensis E. Dean & J. Poore
records.sourceMappingNote: Plazi row 21 contains the source prose spelling talamancesis. The retained sourceColUsageId, treatment taxon ID, sourceScientificName, COL26.8 accepted usage, and WFO crosswalk all identify Lycianthes talamancensis; the dossier uses that exact accepted name without rewriting the retained source row.

morphology.text: Compared with Lycianthes hortulana, the treatment describes L. talamancensis as having longer pedicels (15-22 mm in flower and 27-35 mm in fruit), an entire corolla with moderately hairy adaxial lobes, and longer stamen filaments (1-2 mm).
morphology.placeTimeScope: Comparative diagnosis in the 2020 taxonomic treatment, pages 122-124. The traits are stated relative to L. hortulana and are not estimates of variation across all populations.
morphology.lifeStatus: The claim is bounded to the taxonomic material discussed in the diagnosis; the paragraph does not characterize the provenance or life status of every individual.

distribution.text: The treatment reports L. talamancensis as endemic to Panama, with cited localities in Bocas del Toro and Chiriquí provinces.
distribution.placeTimeScope: As-published distribution statement in the 2020 treatment, pages 122-124; it is not a current exhaustive range survey or an independently validated range map.
distribution.lifeStatus: The article's endemicity and locality wording is reported as attributed; the source does not separately classify every occurrence as wild, cultivated, or escaped.

ecology.text: The treatment associates reported localities with cloud and wet forest at 2,200-2,850 m, and names Quercus, Podocarpus, Magnolia, Symplocos, and Chusquea in the understory context.
ecology.placeTimeScope: Habitat and elevation reported for the treatment's cited localities in Panama, pages 122-124; the named plants are contextual co-occurrences, not asserted as obligate associates.
ecology.lifeStatus: The treatment describes forest settings and taxonomic collections; it does not assess cultivated or escaped populations.

lifeHistory.text: The treatment reports flowering specimens and nearly mature, still-green fruit specimens collected from January through March.
lifeHistory.placeTimeScope: Collection-month summary for specimens cited in the 2020 treatment, pages 122-124; collection months do not establish continuous or complete annual phenology.
lifeHistory.lifeStatus: The statement concerns dated taxonomic specimens; population status and complete seasonal coverage were not assessed.
